name: Brackenfield Town

location.about: A gritstone town of about 140,000 where the Peak District meets the plain: quarries, lead mines, then the railway works and the limestone kilns. A small town with the biggest night in English football in its trophy room - the Crown of Europe, 2004.

colours.story: Moss green and gold - the moss on the gritstone edges above the town and the gold of the bracken in autumn. The first shirts were dyed at a mill in the valley in 1872.

third.shirt: black with moss-green and gold sleeves

rivals.why: the Peak against the city - and the two of them the only East Midlands clubs ever to be champions of Europe (2004 and 2011)
second to Northwick in 1960 and 2003; Brackenfield fans say the 2003 title was won by referees

history.title: The quarrymen's club
history.text: Founded in 1872 by quarrymen and railwaymen. Beaten in the 1874 Founders' Cup final by Holloway Vale, winners in 1885 against Wrexford - then thirty years in and out of the top division: Second Division champions in 1899, 1904 and 1908.

history.title: Champions of England
history.text: Beaten in the Founders' Cup finals of 1920 and 1928 - but champions in 1926, ahead of Northwick, and again in 1934, ahead of Riverton.

history.title: Cups and comebacks
history.text: The Founders' Cup in 1955 (against Penrith); second in 1960, champions in 1961. The Charter Cup in 1968 and 1972. Relegated - and back as Second Division champions in 1974 with a young side that, three years later, won the title (1977, ahead of Ashvale). Down again, up again as champions in 1981, and the Founders' Cup in 1982 against Millbrook.

history.title: The yo-yo years
history.text: Promoted in 1984 and 1994 (both times second), beaten by Oakhurst in the 1988 Charter Cup final - and back-to-back Founders' Cups in 1997 (Millbrook again) and 1998 (Whitcombe). Second in 2003, just behind Northwick.

history.title: The night in Vienna
history.text: Champions of Europe: the Crown of Europe final won against Ajaxia Noord, and that winter the Intercontinental Cup against Boca del Plata. The town's whole population - it seemed - lined the road from the airport.

history.title: Falling and climbing
history.text: Relegated in 2007, back through the play-offs in 2008. Second in 2015 behind Bramhall, beaten in that year's Charter Cup final - and relegated the very next season with the money gone. Back as Division 1 champions in 2018.

honours_note: League seasons are given by the year they ended (1926 = 1925-26).

legends.name: Josiah Bagshaw
legends.note: Quarry foreman; the Bagshaw Stand at the old ground was named after him.

legends.name: Arthur Slack
legends.note: 247 goals - the club record; both 1920s-30s titles.

legends.name: Brian Nuttall
legends.note: From the Second Division to champions in three years.

legends.name: Luka Petrović
legends.note: Lifted the Crown of Europe in 2004.

records.attendance: 53,880 v Riverton Dynamo, League, 1961 (The Delph, before seating)

badge.about: The gritstone edge above the town, crossed quarry hammers, and the star of 2004. Motto 'Ex Rupe Fortitudo' - from the rock, strength.
badge.design: A moss-green shield with a gold border. In the top half a gold silhouette of a rocky gritstone edge with bracken below it; in the bottom half two crossed gold quarry hammers. A single gold star above the shield; 'BRACKENFIELD TOWN' on a gold ribbon below.

ground.name: The Delph

stands.name: Gritstone Stand
stands.features: the main stand, built with the European money: tunnel, dugouts, the Crown of Europe in the trophy room

stands.name: Delph End
stands.features: the home end - a steep single tier cut into the old quarry face, with the rock showing behind the top row

stands.name: Peak Stand
stands.features: two tiers with the gritstone edge and the moors behind

ground.surroundings: built in a worked-out quarry: bare rock behind the home end, the gritstone edge and moors above the town, old lime kilns, the railway viaduct, stone terraces climbing the hill
ground.atmosphere: close and noisy - the quarry walls throw the sound back onto the pitch

for_the_engine.notes: a ground in an old quarry
